questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loose so the wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snug enough to not flap in the wind.
Fit tight so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug enough to not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snug so they do not flap in the wind. They should also be loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. The throttle should:
questions.explanation: Check your throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back quickly when you let go. The clutch should also feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance between you and other vehicles. Maintain this space when following others, being followed, passing, or being passed.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should ensure that it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snug and be free of cracks, loose padding, and frayed straps.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are never very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle. Talk to your doctor about how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets safety standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When traveling at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.
More difficult than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see how far away objects are. At night, artificial lights may not show these clues clearly.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue on long rides, you should:
questions.explanation: Taking rest breaks helps reduce fatigue on long trips. Caffeine may make you more tired when it wears off. Dress warmly and use a windshield to protect yourself from wind and weather, which can also increase fatigue.

questions.question: The best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle is to:
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that it works before every ride.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It affects your steering and balance.
It will disable the front brake.
It will prevent you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering and balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering difficult. This affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing anytime you ride.

questions.question: The front brake should:

options.text: Only be used in an emergency.
Be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chance of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so you do not distract other drivers.

questions.explanation: To avoid a crash, be visible to other drivers, use signals clearly, keep safe distance, watch the road ahead, and identify hazards. Always be ready to react to danger.

questions.question: White lines and yellow lines separate traffic lanes. Which one separates lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has suddenly gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
A discharge of air can be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle's rear tire goes flat, the back may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you most easily.

questions.question: What is the best type of footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.
